paragraphs: Bar Ahina. [Kiddushin 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.9b.18), 51b (compare [Kiddushin 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.51a.10)); [Sotah 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.39b.9): "Rava said: Bar Ahina explained it to me." Hyman also gives his name as Rava. [Menachot 37b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.37b.9): "Rav Yosef said, etc."; "Rava bar Ahina said, etc." — or perhaps, Hyman suggests, the text should read: "Rava said," "Bar Ahina said."[^2]

notes.text: The consulted Menachot 37b reads Rava bar Ahina together. The proposed division into two speakers is Hyman’s conjecture.

[Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=257&lang=en) cites 51a as well as 9b and Sotah 39b for Bar Ahina explaining a teaching to Rava. The consulted Menachot gives Rava bar Ahina as one name. Hyman tentatively proposes two speakers there.
